watson: In the year 1878 I took my degree of Doctor of Medicine of the University of London.
The campaign brought honours and promotion to many, but for me it had nothing but misfortune and disaster.
Worn with pain, and weak from the prolonged hardships which I had undergone, I was removed to the base hospital.
I had neither kith nor kin in England, and was therefore as free as air.
There I stayed for some time at a private hotel in the Strand, leading a comfortless, meaningless existence.
So alarming did the state of my finances become, that I soon realized that I must make a complete alteration in my style of living.
